styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin strip: two pale horizontal bands between brown side posts, with a narrow green cap on top. Each material has only about 2-3 lightness steps. The bands are smooth, with none of the per-stone shading, grain or speckle that the paving reference has on every cobble. The dark edges are partly neutral (41% near-neutral) and read as a uniform sticker-like line, not a dark tone of the neighbouring material. The measured 6 visible tones per tile is above the grass reference (3) and just under the paving reference (7). The raw numbers (14 colours in total, 6 per tile) show a small, flat palette, and by eye the strip is much thinner and flatter than either reference. It also reads more like a rail or fence than steps cut into a cliff face, with no cliff rock or step depth. A careful artist would not accept it beside the Beodeul references.
